neighbours.label: An afterthought word that closes a clause after its predicate (', of course.', ', really,', 'himself,', 'now.', 'at first'): a trailing comment or reflexive emphasis, not the same word placed at the start of the clause
fire: The plan was doomed from the start, of course. Nobody said so out loud.
It's strange, really, how quickly people forget a crisis.
She was a skilled sailor herself, so she knew the risk.
He was a grandfather now. The house felt different with a baby in it.
The wine seems sharp at first, but it softens in the glass.
I think the whole story was invented anyway. It never added up.
The answer was obvious, of course, once someone pointed it out.
It's sad, really, that the old theatre closed.
quiet: Of course the plan was doomed from the start. Nobody said so out loud.
Really, it is strange how quickly people forget a crisis.
She knew the risk because she had sailed for years.
Now he was a grandfather. The house felt different with a baby in it.
At first the wine seems sharp, but it softens in the glass.
Anyway, I think the whole story was invented. It never added up.
Of course the answer was obvious once someone pointed it out.
Honestly, the closing of the old theatre made everyone sad.

predictions: Clause-final 'of course', 'really', 'anyway', 'himself/herself', 'now', 'at first' reach 0.5-0.9. Twin sentences with the same word moved to the front of the clause stay under 0.15.
